literal: Modesty called one thing we do not know, if by love those who cherished (us) do pleasing things.
translation: We know nothing of a thing called modesty, if our beloved, out of love, acts in ways that please us.
modern: நம்மை விரும்பிய காதலர், காதலினால் நமக்கு விருப்பமானவற்றைச் செய்யும்போது, நாணம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு குணத்தை நாம் அறியமாட்டோம்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine describes how her natural reserve and modesty completely dissolve in the warmth of her lover's affection. She states that when her beloved, whom she deeply cherishes, acts out of love to do things that please her, she loses all awareness of what is called modesty ('நாண்'). The word 'பெட்ப' refers to pleasing or desirable actions that bring joy. The verse highlights how the overwhelming power of mutual love ('காமம்') naturally overcomes any sense of restraint or hesitation.
